hypotheses.latent_object: Two-index summand kernel L2(h1_label, h2_labels; beta, gamma, mu, epsilon(n), epsilon(m)) whose coefficient depends only on beta, gamma, mu, epsilon(m), epsilon(n) and whose h1/h2 label arguments can be permuted b <-> c.
proof_obligations: Substituting b <-> c in the h1/h2 arguments of G0002 yields exactly the summand of G0006.
hypotheses.rationale: The two 2-index sums have the same coefficient expression and differ only by permutation of the source labels b and c carried by h1 and h2.

hypotheses.latent_object: Off-diagonal coefficient kernel K_offdiag(b,c; epsilon_m, epsilon_n) = expression in G0005 before summing.
proof_obligations: limit(expr(G0005), epsilon(m), epsilon(n)) == expr(G0004) for fixed epsilon(n), beta, gamma, mu
required_assumptions: The limit exists and polygamma arguments avoid singularities.
hypotheses.rationale: The piecewise diagonal branch is the confluent limit of the m != n branch as epsilon(m) approaches epsilon(n); denominators in G0005 are powers of epsilon(m)-epsilon(n).

hypotheses.latent_object: Off-diagonal coefficient kernel K_offdiag(c,b; epsilon_m, epsilon_n) = expression in G0009 before summing.
proof_obligations: limit(expr(G0009), epsilon(m), epsilon(n)) == expr(G0008) for fixed epsilon(n), beta, gamma, mu
required_assumptions: The limit exists and polygamma arguments avoid singularities.
hypotheses.rationale: The second 2-index family is the b/c-permuted copy of the first, so its diagonal branch is likewise the confluent limit of its off-diagonal branch.

hypotheses.latent_object: Three-index off-diagonal kernel K3(h1(a,m,n), h1(b,ell,m), h1(c,n,ell)) = expression in G0016 before summing.
proof_obligations: limit(G0016, epsilon(m)->epsilon(n)) == G0013 with epsilon(ell) fixed
limit(G0016, epsilon(ell)->epsilon(n)) == G0014 with epsilon(m) fixed
limit(G0016, epsilon(ell)->epsilon(m)) == G0015 with epsilon(n) fixed
required_assumptions: All identified limits exist and avoid polygamma singularities.
hypotheses.rationale: The whole 3-index piecewise branch set is generated by coalescences of the spectral parameters epsilon(ell), epsilon(m), epsilon(n) from the totally non-coincident branch G0016.
